serpapi is now predictable for scripts and AI agents, and safe on a terminal.

- **One error contract.** Errors and warnings are JSON lines on stderr with the HTTP status. Exit 2 means fix the command; it fails before a billed search, except when a `--jq` filter fails on the response itself; 1 is an API or network error; 130 means Ctrl-C or SIGTERM stopped it before it finished, after printing what had arrived.
- **Markdown and other formats.** `output=md`, `html`, `plain` and `csv`, in any case, work for `search` and `archive` (#10).
- **Timeouts.** `--timeout` takes seconds, such as `120`, or a duration, such as `2m`; `SERPAPI_TIMEOUT` sets it for a shell; `0` waits indefinitely. The default is 60 s (#15, @strzibny).
- **`--all-pages`.** `--fields` no longer stops paging after page 1 (#9, @adarshdigievo). `no_cache`, `zero_trace` and `output` apply to every page. Paging stops at a repeated page or at a page a mistyped `--fields` matches nothing on. Pages already fetched are printed, through `--jq` too, when a later page fails or on Ctrl-C. Output streams, so 100 pages of 1 MiB peak at 187–188 MiB instead of 720–735 MiB (3 runs each against v0.2.3 on macOS arm64, from a local fake API).
- **Warnings that name the fix.** A large result lists its top-level keys by size and the free `serpapi archive ID --jq` next step, or says when `no_cache` or `zero_trace` makes a repeat a new, counted search. A `--jq` that prints only null lists the keys the response has. A parameter given twice says which value was sent.
- **Safer.** Terminal output escapes control characters from results and from the account email that `login` prints, so a page title can't set the clipboard or clear the screen. `serpapi account` masks the API key (#7, @ilyazub), and the key is never echoed from a stray argument or a broken config file. `login` saves the key only under an absolute HOME, through a new private temp file, so a file left at the old temp name can't widen its permissions or receive the key. Ctrl-C or SIGTERM at its prompts stops it at once with echo on.
- **Also:** `serpapi version`; `login --api-key`; `login` asks before replacing a saved key (#7); `SERPAPI_API_KEY` as a fallback for `SERPAPI_KEY`; `--help` documents exit codes, errors and costs.
- **Patched Go.** Binaries are built with the latest patched Go at release time; `go version -m "$(command -v serpapi)"` shows which. v0.2.3's binaries were built with go1.25.0, in which `govulncheck -mode=binary` finds 57 (darwin/arm64) and 58 (linux/amd64) known vulnerabilities; a release rehearsal with go1.27.2 found none.

## Changes scripts may notice

- These now exit 2 before any request: `q=` with bare words, no parameters, the API key passed as `key`, `apikey`, `serp_api_key` or `serpapi_key` (`api_key` already did), `--fields` outside `search`, `--max-pages 0`, `--all-pages` with `async=true`, `--jq` or `--all-pages` with `output=md`, an unknown `output=`, and `locations` without a query.
- A `--jq` filter that can't run, such as a syntax error, `input` or `debug`, fails before the search; one that fails on the response, such as `tonumber` on a title, still exits 2 after it. `halt` now works.
- Bare words are joined into one `q`: `serpapi search engine=google coffee shops` sends `q=coffee shops`, not `q=shops`.
- `--fields` adds `error` to `json_restrictor`, so an API error still arrives. `--fields ,,` sends no `json_restrictor`; it used to send `,,` and print `{}`.
- A `SERPAPI_KEY` padded with spaces or a newline is trimmed before it's sent.
- `serpapi account` prints `api_key` masked, as `abcd…wxyz` (#7).
- `--all-pages`: when a later page fails, or `serpapi_pagination.next` isn't a valid URL, the pages so far are printed before the error, exit 1; that invalid URL is now `api_error`, not `network_error`. A 200 response with an error on a later page is a warning after the pages so far, exit 0, not exit 1.
- A JSON array body is exit 1 `api_error`, not exit 0.
- `serpapi` with no command prints nothing on stdout, where its usage used to go; stderr has the JSON error, and the usage too on a terminal. It still exits 2.
- `serpapi help TOPIC` with an unknown topic exits 2 with a JSON `usage_error` naming the closest command; it exited 0 with the usage on stderr.
- `serpapi login` exits 2 when HOME (`%AppData%` on Windows) isn't an absolute path, and no command reads a config file then; v0.2.3 used `.config/serpapi` under the current directory.
- At the hidden key prompt, Ctrl-D exits 2 with "No API key given" (v0.2.3 kept waiting), and SIGTERM exits 130 with echo on (v0.2.3: 143, echo off).
- The default timeout is 60 s, not 30 s.

Thanks to @adarshdigievo (#4, #9), @jvmvik (#6), @strzibny (#15) and @ilyazub (#7).
